test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Upper House of the Parliament of India?

options.text: It is dissolved after every 5 years.
It is dissolved after every 6 years.
It is dissolved after every 3 years.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is never dissolved.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Upper House of the Parliament of India is also known as the Rajya Sabha.
 
• It is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha have a term of six years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.
 
• This ensures that the Rajya Sabha is a continuous body, unlike the Lok Sabha, which is dissolved every five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of India's Parliament, representing the states and union territories.
 
• It was constituted on April 3, 1952, and held its first session on May 13, 1952.
 
• The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is 250 members, out of which 238 are representatives of states and union territories, and 12 are nominated by the President for their expertise in specific fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the Lower House of India's Parliament, also known as the House of the People.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 members: 530 from the states, 20 from union territories.
 
• The term of the Lok Sabha is five years, after which it is dissolved unless extended during a national emergency.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Procedure**
 
 
• Both houses of Parliament play a crucial role in the legislative process, including the introduction, discussion, and passing of bills.
 
• A bill can be introduced in either house, except for money bills, which must be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
 
• After a bill is passed by both houses, it is sent to the President for assent, after which it becomes law.
